title: Course 12 checkpoint — Enterprise AI Operating Model and Leadership

questions.prompt: A prohibited use case has exceptional expected value. What should portfolio intake do?
options: Ask the model to approve it
questions.explanation: A prohibited or otherwise non-compensatory boundary gates the candidate; expected value cannot create authority or acceptable risk.

questions.prompt: A proposal has no current outcome-confidence evidence. Which disposition is most accurate?
options: Assign confidence zero and rank it
questions.explanation: Missing proof is an explicit evidence gap; referral or a bounded experiment preserves uncertainty instead of inventing a measured value.

questions.prompt: In a federated AI operating model, who normally owns the domain product outcome?
questions.explanation: Domain teams retain user, workflow, evidence, adoption and outcome ownership while shared teams provide reusable contracts and controls.

questions.prompt: What is the main defect in a decision matrix with three accountable owners?
options: Final accountability and escalation are ambiguous
questions.explanation: Consultation can be broad, but one accountable authority is required so a decision, response deadline and escalation path remain clear.

questions.prompt: Which property makes a paved road a supported product rather than a mandate?
options: Consumer outcome, SLO, support, lifecycle, unit cost and exit path
questions.explanation: A paved road earns adoption through a complete service contract and useful experience while preserving a governed path for unsupported needs.

questions.prompt: A candidate changes data source after an exception is approved. Can the old receipt be reused?
questions.explanation: An exception binds the exact candidate version, policy, control, rationale and compensating controls; a material subject change requires new review.

questions.prompt: Eight capability dimensions are scalable and people capability is provisional. What should the overall assessment communicate?
options: The provisional floor and its limiting evidence
Ignore people because it is qualitative
questions.explanation: A readiness claim must expose the weakest relevant capability instead of averaging away a constraint that can prevent safe operation or adoption.

questions.prompt: What makes a roadmap initiative testable rather than a feature promise?
options: Owner, baseline, target, resources, dependencies, exit and kill criteria
questions.explanation: A testable initiative binds an accountable owner and measurable change to resource and sequencing assumptions plus explicit continuation boundaries.

questions.prompt: Why use low, base and high investment scenarios?
options: To expose adoption, cost and benefit sensitivity rather than present false precision
questions.explanation: Scenario ranges keep consequential uncertainty visible and show whether the decision remains defensible when adoption, timing, benefits or costs vary.

questions.prompt: A reviewer raises an evidence-backed objection that remains unresolved. What should the decision record do?
options: Preserve it, record the accountable response and assign escalation or accepted risk
Give the reviewer automatic production authority
questions.explanation: Durable dissent supports learning and accountability; status, unresolved risk, response and escalation prevent both erasure and indefinite veto.

questions.prompt: Which statement is a sound delegation boundary?
options: Draft and defend the service standard; production approval remains with the control owner
You are accountable but have no resources
questions.explanation: Effective delegation names the objective and bounded decision space while preserving authorities that were not delegated and supplying support and review.

questions.prompt: Why should platform adoption not be the only success metric?
options: Forced or superficial use may rise without better experience, reliability, compliant outcomes or value
questions.explanation: Adoption is an intermediate behavior that can be gamed; it must be interpreted with consumer experience, delivery, reliability, safety and outcome measures.
